Lessons.Title: Solving Quadratic Equations by Using Factored Form
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: transform a quadratic equality to an expression equal zero, factor the expression and use the zero-product property to solve all real roots; check answers in the ORIGINAL equation. Independently authored Edulytiks adaptation of Illustrative Mathematics Algebra 1 First Edition Unit 7 Lesson 9 teacher https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/7/9/preparation.html and student https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/students/1/7/9/index.html (CC BY 4.0). The source connects factoring with questions previously answered only by graphs.
Original equation x²+4x=12. Subtract12 to obtain x²+4x−12=0. Find factor constants6 and−2, sum4 product−12: (x+6)(x−2)=0. Roots x−6 and x2. Check x−6:36−24=12; x2:4+8=12.

Do not factor x²+4x directly and set x=0 or x−4 without handling right side12. Zero-product property requires a zero product. Graphically, the solutions are x-coordinates of intersections between y=x²+4x and horizontal line y=12. Equivalently they are zeros of y=x²+4x−12.

Student task: solve three equations with nonzero right sides via equal-zero transformation, graph one to confirm intersections, and critique a peer's invalid zero-product step. Teacher-scored rubric0–2 for valid rearrangement, correct factorization, both roots and complete verification.

KeyConcepts.Title: Move target to zero
KeyConcepts.Definition: Subtract same quantity from both sides before using factors.

KeyConcepts.Title: Factoring to solve
KeyConcepts.Definition: Convert zero polynomial to product and solve each factor.

KeyConcepts.Title: Graph intersection
KeyConcepts.Definition: Equation f(x)=12 means intersections with horizontal y=12.

WorkedExamples.Title: Solve x²+4x=12
WorkedExamples.Question: Find all real roots.
WorkedExamples.Method: Show distributive or equivalence-preserving algebra and independently verify every candidate solution.

WorkedExamples.Title: Explain graph interpretation
WorkedExamples.Question: Which graph intersections correspond to the equation?
WorkedExamples.Method: Show distributive or equivalence-preserving algebra and independently verify every candidate solution.
Steps: Their intersection x-coordinates solve original equation.

WorkedExamples.Title: Refute early zero-product
WorkedExamples.Question: Does setting x(x+4)=0 solve x²+4x=12?
WorkedExamples.Method: Show distributive or equivalence-preserving algebra and independently verify every candidate solution.
Steps: The original has left product x(x+4) equal12, not0.
Subtract12 before factoring correct zero equation.
WorkedExamples.Answer: No; it would solve a different equation.

CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: A sign error could change roots.

SummaryPoints: Rearrange to zero, factor, solve factors and check.
